ai.seo_question: How is the divorce of a mentally unstable person handled in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal status of a man with intermittent mental instability (*mudajjan*), ruling that his guardian (*wali*) holds authority over him akin to the Imam's authority over the general populace. This establishes that such an individual is not considered fully competent to execute his own divorce, as his inconsistent state prevents reliable determination of his intent, thereby necessitating the guardian's oversight to ensure validity.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Abu Al Abbas Al Razzaz, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Al Fazal Bin Shazan, altogether from safwan, from Abu Khalid Al qammat who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man whose opinion is recognised at one time, and denied another, is the divorce of his guardian allowed over him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is the matter with him that he does not divorce (himself)?’ I said, ‘He does not know the limit of the divorce, and is not secure upon it, if he divorces today, but he would be saying tomorrow, ‘I did not divorce’’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not see him except being at the status of the Imam, meaning the guardian’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and abu al-‘Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayyub ibn Nuh and Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ‘Abd Allah from Safwan from abu Khalid al-Qammat who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who sometime understands and sometimes does not understand: if his divorce by his guardian is permissible. He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is the matter with him, why does he not divorce?’ I replied, ‘He does not know the rules of divorce and does not feel safe. Perhaps tomorrow he will say that he did not divorce.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not see him (guardian) except like an Imam (in his case).”’
